title: ScanEval case pack
description: A namespaced, versioned set of pinned snapshots and case records. Public and organization-owned packs share this contract. Labels become scoring evidence only through recorded human review; nothing here is a scanner input.

review_budgets.description: The cut-offs every recall-at-k number is computed at, copied into each plan by scaneval.cases.build_plan. Inside anchor_sha256, because editing a budget changes what a run reports about a scanner without changing a single label.

anchor_sha256.description: The digest of every record a planning decision reads that no other record already holds: the pack fields themselves, review_budgets included, each snapshot, each case minus its notes, and the chain value the admission history ends at. Computed by scaneval.contracts.pack_anchor_digest, which projects the whole record minus a stated allowlist rather than a list of fields to cover, so a field added to this schema is anchored the day it is added. Two subtractions are made for a digest that already exists, and only while it does. A case's label fields are left out while its latest recorded review carries a labels_sha256 over them, so that an edited label costs the approval rather than an anchor a person would have to rebuild before re-approving; a case no review has bound, a draft or a mechanically checked one, is anchored with its target, its controls, its evidence, and what it says it represents, because no digest holds those. A snapshot's identity is left out only for a snapshot some case names, and only once every case in the pack binds its own labels. A label digest carries the identity of the snapshots that label names and of no others, so a snapshot the pack declares that no case names is inside no digest however thoroughly the rest of the pack is reviewed, and until every case binds, some case reads those bytes with no digest speaking for them. Both halves are asked per snapshot by scaneval.contracts.snapshots_bound_by_labels. Every pack carries one: the field is optional here only so that a pack without it is refused by the rule that says why rather than by a shape error, and a pack that omits it is refused all the same, because an optional anchor is no anchor. Editing the disposition that keeps a case in a plan, deleting a case's mechanical check set, rewriting the review budgets a recall-at-k number is computed at, deleting a whole case with its chained review history, wiping a case's review history so an empty one is indistinguishable from a deleted one, deleting the admission that kept a case out of a plan, and repinning or re-declaring the languages of a snapshot no label digest holds each leave the pack anchoring to something else. Anyone who can edit the pack can recompute this, so it makes such a deletion visible rather than impossible.

reference.description: How the commit was chosen: tag, parent of fix, or explicit advisory commit.

languages.description: Which adapters are run against this export, and therefore part of the snapshot identity scaneval.contracts.label_digest covers: a snapshot re-declared as holding no Python is a different scan of the same bytes, and an approval that covered the one did not cover the other. Read as a set, so the order carries no content.

decision.description: unresolved records the reviewer reopening the question rather than settling it. The latest recorded review is the operative one: a case whose latest review rejected it or left it unresolved is not currently approved, so it cannot be recorded as human_approved, planning leaves it out, and the whole recorded history stays in place. Rejection and reopening are one rule, scaneval.contracts.operative_review_gap, which the load, the planning gate, and record_review all read.

labels_sha256.description: Digest of the label content this review covers: what the case claims to be, its target, every control, and the identity of every snapshot those name, projected by scaneval.contracts.label_digest. An approval covers the exact bytes reviewed, so a snapshot repinned to another commit or another exported tree changes this digest exactly as an edited label does. The latest review whose digest equals the case's current labels is the one review every gate asks, both for whether the approval stands and for what the validation level is. Absent on reviews recorded before approvals were bound to content; such a review is read as covering no current label, so planning leaves the case out until a review of the labels as they stand, and while the latest review is one of those the pack anchor covers the label fields instead, because nothing else does.

chain_sha256.description: This review's place in the chain: the digest of its own fields together with the chain value of the review recorded before it, computed by scaneval.contracts.review_chain_digest. Every recorded review carries one, and a pack whose chain does not verify is refused, so deleting the review that withdrew an approval cannot quietly restore it. Anyone who can edit the pack can recompute the chain, so this is not a signature and says nothing about who recorded a review; what it removes is the deletion that passes unnoticed.

check.description: One mechanical (L1) check result, and one member of the check set recorded for the snapshot it names. snapshot_id is required: a check that belongs to no set is a check no record accounts for, and dropping the field would take a failing check out of its set.

evidence.description: The records a label rests on. Inside scaneval.contracts.label_digest: an allegation at a reviewed level is the allegation together with its evidence, so deleting an advisory or rewriting what one says costs the approval exactly as an edited target does. Read in evidence_id order, which the contract keeps unique, so the order of the list carries no content.

disposition.description: The screening decision build_plan reads: an excluded case is not planned. Inside anchor_sha256, so dropping an approved and admitted case out of a plan by editing two scalars is a pack that no longer anchors to its own records.

level.description: A cached copy of the level the case's own records establish, never a fact in its own right and never read to decide anything. For a human_approved case that level is the level of the one review covering the labels as they stand, and this field must be exactly it: a value above or below that review is refused, so a case cannot be recorded at L2 under an L4 curator approval and then planned at L4. That covering review must also earn what it records, which for L3 and L4 means it was itself made by an independent_reviewer. For a mechanically_checked case the level is L1, and a draft carries none. L3 and L4 also require disposition validate, because a reviewed label rests on the screening decision behind it.

review_state.description: mechanically_checked means level L1 and a recorded passing check set, carrying snapshot_id, for every snapshot the case references; it is never a claim that a person read anything. This field and the latest recorded review are two records of one fact and must agree in both directions. human_approved requires the latest recorded review to be an approving one: a rejection and an unresolved reopening are both withdrawals, and both leave the case at the state its mechanical checks earn. Equally, a case recorded draft or mechanically_checked under a latest review that approved it is refused: withdrawing an approval is a decision a named reviewer records, not an edited scalar.

check_sets.description: One record per mechanical check set, keyed by the snapshot_id it ran against. The set is this record, never the checks that happen to carry a snapshot id: result is what the set decided, tree_hash is the export it read, and checks_sha256 covers both together with every check of the set, so deleting a failing check, unattributing one, reordering two, or editing one no longer turns a failed set into a passing one. Absent when the case records no check set. tree_hash is also the third of three records of one fact, beside the detail of the set's passing snapshot_hash_recorded check and the snapshot's declared tree_hash, and loading a pack requires all three to agree: editing any two contradicts the third instead of retargeting a standing check set, or an approval resting on one, at a different export. A failing set records the export it read and rejected, which the declared hash is not expected to match.

checks_failed.description: Absent by default. Set when a mechanical check set failed for a snapshot this case references after the case was human approved: the recorded review and level stand, and planning leaves the case out until a correction decision resolves it.

reviews_sha256.description: Where the recorded review history ends: the chain_sha256 of its last review, present exactly when the case records a review. The chain binds each review to the one before it, which catches an edit, a reordering, and a deletion from the middle; this catches the deletion off the end, which is the one that would otherwise restore an approval by dropping the review that withdrew it. Anyone who can edit the pack can rewrite this too, so it makes a deletion visible rather than impossible.

admission.description: One admission decision made by a named person. It names both the case it was recorded on and the target_id that case carried at the time; the target_id is inside the label digest, so the decision is bound to content a review covers rather than to a name. A pack whose admission no longer resolves to the target of the case it names is refused, and planning routes each decision by target_id, so renaming two cases cannot move a rejection onto different content. Only an explicit admitted decision admits: a case with no recorded decision, or one recorded deferred, is planned as a draft and never reaches a reviewed-scope plan.

chain_sha256.description: This decision's place in the admission chain: the digest of its own fields together with the chain value of the decision recorded before it, computed by scaneval.contracts.admission_chain_digest. Every recorded admission carries one, and the pack anchor records where the chain ends, so deleting the rejection that kept a case out of a plan cannot quietly restore it, from the middle of the history or off the end.
